notes.note:
After taking a quick look on the pcap/log, it seems that the issue comes from the fact that the InitialUEMessage/Deregistration request is sending with a new RAN-UE-NGAP-ID (value 27) without AMF-UE-NGAP-ID which basically for a new UE/connection (instead of using the current one with RAN-UE-NGAP-ID 26 and AMF-UE-NGAP-ID 7 for the current connection). Probably due to the  AN release procedure  just before (packet No. 540, 542, 543) so there's no N2 UE context in both gNB and AMF side. 

Let me double-check 3GPP specification to make sure that AMF behaves correctly. thanks

notes.note: I'd respectfully note that keeping in RAM all deregistered UEs is a bad solution as (1) as already mentioned, it can fill the RAM and lead to a DOS, and (2) for forensics it is bad too as it wipes the state as soon as the same UE re-registers, and also when the AMF is recycled. The good solution is to store on disk, in other words, logging. And if you really need a fast enumeration of "all UEs seen from the beginning of time", it is easy to get it as an asynchronous log post-processing. If you need an O(1) lookup of "what is the current status of UE x ?", again, there are plenty of techniques for off-line log indexing.
